stories.summary: Two Nvidia investors with about $2.13 billion of stock disclosed as of June 30 are calling for a deliberate leadership search after Huang’s resignation.

sources.title: Nvidia board urged to consider 'potential return of Jensen Huang' by two major investors
sources.text: Two major Nvidia shareholders are calling on the board of directors to weigh all options for the company's future leadership, including "the potential return of Jensen Huang." Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner posted a letter on X on Friday that urges Nvidia's board to "pursue a slow, measured, and deliberate process regarding the future leadership of Nvidia." The letter is also signed by Atreides Management's Gavin Baker. Nvidia was Altimeter Capital's largest disclosed equity holding in its most recent SEC filing , with a 9.4 million-share stake worth nearly $1.9 billion as of June 30. Atreides held 1.2 million shares worth nearly $250 million at the end of June. The letter said Nvidia will be "capably led" by interim CEO Colette Kress , who served as Nvidia's CFO for 13 years before the board announced Thursday that she'd lead the company in Huang's absence. "But the Founder and long time incredible leader of this extraordinary company has earned the right for a deliberate process that avoids any needless rush to replace him before all the facts are known," the letter concludes. The document did not call for Huang's immediate reinstatement. Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday amid multiple affair allegations, including one with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang , who also worked with Nvidia customer Megaspeed . The Singapore-based company is being investigated by the Justice Department for possibly redirecting some of its supply of Nvidia's restricted artificial intelligence chips to China. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said on X Friday that he signed a petition asking to reinstate Huang. A petition circulating online called "Stand with Jensen" claims to have more than 100,000 signatures, including more than 5,000 current Nvidia employees. Musk said on X Saturday that without Huang, some "critical deals will be lost." Another letter sent Friday called on U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick to testify about Megaspeed before the House Intelligence Committee. Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10 about whether the Commerce Department is "properly performing its broader role of preventing China from acquiring advanced AI chips," according to the letter. Huang has also been asked to testify . The Commerce Department originally launched an investigation into Megaspeed that was moved to the Justice Department in 2025 after Nvidia's lawyer contacted a senior Commerce official, according to The New York Times. President Donald Trump is scheduled to visit China on Thursday, but doesn't plan to raise Nvidia and the suspected spy affair during his meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping , according to U.S. officials. Musk is expected to join Trump on the trip to Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit on Nov. 18 and 19.

sources.title: Tech world's calls for Jensen Huang to return to Nvidia are growing
sources.text: An online petition calling for Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO of Nvidia has drawn more than 170,000 signatures, as prominent tech executives, employees and shareholders rally behind the chipmaker's co-founder following his resignation last week. The "Stand with Jensen " campaign has attracted support from Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, according to the petition's website, which notes that affiliations are self-reported and not verified. Some other high-profile signatories include Shopify's CEO Tobias Lütke, Hugging Face's CEO Julien Chaumond, and robotic startup Atoms' CEO Travis Kalanick. Dozens of current and former Nvidia employees also signed the petition. Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993 and helped turn it into a dominant supplier of artificial intelligence chips, resigned as Nvidia's president, CEO and board member last week following reports of extramarital affairs — including one involving a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence. Nvidia appointed longtime finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO and said its board would consider both internal and external candidates in its search for a permanent successor. The growing campaign to reinstate Huang adds a layer of complexity to the decision for Nvidia's board as it looks to put the controversy behind it, and coincides with reports that he is considering a comeback. Any potential return, however, faces significant hurdles. Nvidia's board is continuing an independent investigation into the conduct that led to Huang's departure. What's more, U.S. lawmakers are preparing for investigations into how the now-ex-CEO's affair may have damaged America's artificial intelligence dominance, the national security implications and the executive's close relationship with President Donald Trump and his Cabinet. Musk was among the most prominent tech executives to publicly back Huang's reinstatement, saying on X that he would sign a petition calling for the former Nvidia chief's return. "A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I'm signing it too," Musk wrote on X. He had previously also said it would be "an honor" to hire Huang. The campaign has drawn support from people identifying themselves as current and former Nvidia employees, shareholders and business partners, according to the petition's website. It calls on Nvidia's board to ensure a fair investigation into Huang's conduct and provide greater transparency around the circumstances of his departure. Some Nvidia employees have also publicly expressed support for Huang, with one engineer saying he had decided to leave the company following the CEO's departure. Darrell Dai, who identified himself as a robotics engineer at Nvidia, said Huang's vision and the engineering culture he fostered were key reasons he had stayed at the company. Another Nvidia employee, Vartika Singh, who said she had worked at the chipmaker for nearly eight years, praised Huang's leadership and personal support during a family medical crisis. "I have never worked for anyone quite like Jensen Huang, and I doubt I ever will," Singh wrote on X, describing his commitment to employees, researchers and startups. The push has also gained traction among major shareholders, with Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management's Gavin Baker urging Nvidia's board to consider all options, including Huang's potential return, in an open letter Friday. The investors called for a measured approach to choosing Nvidia's next leader, arguing that Huang deserved a fair process before the board made any permanent decision. Neil Shah, vice president of research at Counterpoint Research, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Monday that a potential Huang comeback would be "good for the stock." "Jensen's rhythm has made this AI ecosystem what it is right now," Shah told CNBC's Karen Tso and Steve Sedgwick. "The trillion-dollar capex, which has been spent every year, has to continue to make this train [keep] going." Shah said his only concern is whether Nvidia would impose new guardrails on Huang, preventing him from leading the business with the same level of energy and enthusiasm. "If he cannot work freely and actually take the ecosystem on the same breadth and speed, will he be that effective? That is the big question." Huang has discussed the possibility of returning as Nvidia's chief executive with close confidants, the Financial Times reported , citing multiple people familiar with the matter. One of his allies told the FT that supporters were assembling a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for his reinstatement and would seek backing from the White House. The efforts had Huang's support, the person added, according to the report. "We are in the process of selecting a search firm for the NVIDIA CEO role. We have not formally engaged any potential candidates," an Nvidia spokesperson said in response to CNBC's request for comment on the company's search. The spokesperson added that any speculation about individual candidates, whether internal or external, was premature. Anthony Scaramucci, founder of alternative investment firm SkyBridge and a former White House communications director, also dismissed the prospect of Huang returning as CEO, saying the investigations surrounding him presented obstacles that a public campaign could not overcome. "The tech bros want Jensen back. Not happening," Scaramucci wrote on X, arguing that Nvidia's board could not reinstate a chief executive whose conduct remained under investigation. In a separate post , Scaramucci rejected comparisons with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who returned to the company days after being ousted in 2023. "The FBI doesn't take petitions," he wrote, saying that Huang's situation was fundamentally different from Altman's. Altman's ouster stemmed from an internal governance dispute, while Huang's situation involves ongoing investigations into his conduct that make a swift board reversal

sources.title: Elon Musk, other tech execs sign petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang
sources.text: A petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate the company’s recently ousted CEO Jensen Huang appears to have attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon. The petition website said the signers include 5,965 current Nvidia employees, 1,108 former employees, and 63,063 shareholders. Notable supporters include Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan. The petition states that its signers are “concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process” and demands that the board “bring him back while an independent investigation establishes the facts.” It also calls on the board to ensure a fair investigation and provide more information to the public. “Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice,” the petition says. Huang resigned on Thursday , four days after confessing to having an affair with a chip executive suspected by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy. The former CEO has agreed to testify before Congress, while news reports have also suggested that Huang engaged in multiple extramarital affairs . Nvidia appointed CFO Colette Kress as the company’s interim CEO while it searches for a permanent replacement. Nvidia’s stock price fell sharply through the week, while Huang’s departure is also expected to leave a big gap in AI industry funding . sources.title: Jensen Huang and the decline of the visionary showman founder CEO
sources.text: The Steve Jobs of GPUs has been shown the door.﻿ On January 6th, 2025, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang got his rockstar moment at last. He strode triumphantly onstage, hand raised in the air, to the claps and cheers of a 14,000-person arena absolutely packed with influencers and fans, their faces awash in blue glow, as he made his entrance in a black leather jacket that shimmered in the stadium’s lights. Few are cheering for Jensen Huang now. He has left Nvidia after seemingly enabling two chip smuggling scandals and allegedly having three extramarital affairs , including one with an alleged Chinese spy at the same time he was mingling with President Donald Trump. The world is watching to see if this scandal might disrupt the entire US AI industry and perhaps destabilize the stock market along with it. That’s because Huang wasn’t merely running the first $5 trillion company , he was the visionary leader in control of the must-have GPUs powering the worldwide AI boom, part of a company that represents around 6 percent of the S&P 500 stock market index all by itself. And he didn’t plan for succession if he ever stepped down. The 63-year-old once said he preferred to die on the job ; he once suggested he’d work until he was 90 or 100 , then carry on leading the company as a robot. It’s not easy to replace Huang, partly because he had no deputies. Around 60 employees reported directly to the CEO . “He built the company around himself, and everything that happened there flowed through him,” says IDC analyst and former computing journalist Tom Mainelli. “Jensen is Nvidia, and Nvidia is Jensen,” Jon Peddie, a computer industry analyst who’s been tracking Nvidia since its inception, tells me. But Nvidia isn’t Jensen anymore. He has left the company he cofounded 33 years ago. It’s the end of an era, and not just for Nvidia — because Jensen Huang was Big Tech’s last true example of a visionary showman founder CEO. “He was both the visionary and the tactical leader, the closest thing tech has had to Steve Jobs,” Moor Insights & Strategy chief analyst Pat Moorhead tells me. Elon Musk didn’t exactly found Tesla and has quite the track record of broken promises, and Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg has proven to be neither visionary nor showman so far. Google’s Larry Page and Sergey Brin stepped away in 2019 as their company dealt with growing employee turmoil , leaving the company in the hands of Sundar Pichai, and both Microsoft and Apple have each passed the torch twice since the days of Bill Gates and Steve Jobs. Some say Apple’s Steve Jobs broke the CEO mold, but he created a mold of his own. Huang was one of countless tech leaders who followed his example by introducing their products in keynote speeches, adopting a single recognizable piece of clothing like Jobs’ trademark black turtleneck, and even occasionally teasing “one more thing” for the surprise at the end of their presentations. In the newsroom, we’d sometimes joke about the Jobs wannabes; many were stiff suits who didn’t have the credibility to pull it off. I thought Huang might be a Jobs wannabe, too, the first time I saw that he’d adopted a black jacket as his uniform. (It was not always a leather jacket; an earlier version was a Nvidia-branded softshell.) Huang later insisted on wearing a jacket even when the temperature was hot — more than once, I saw him sweat profusely rather than take it off. Unlike Jobs, he also held quite a few keynotes when he didn’t have much news to share; he liked to repeat the company’s previous accomplishments as if they were brand-new. But even if Huang didn’t have the same gravitas as Jobs, he did have exciting tech up his sleeves and loved to demo it onstage. He knew how to get people excited about the future of visual computing with eye-opening gaming graphics, physics and lighting demos, and eventually image recognition, AI weather simulations, digital copies of real-world factories, and the robots that can virtually train in them. His Nvidia tried to educate people about the how and why of GPUs, too; I still remember in 2008 when Nvidia invited the Mythbusters to demo the difference between serial processing and parallel processing by firing a 1,100-nozzle paintball gun to “paint” the Mona Lisa in one shot. What I didn’t know back then: Huang was a visionary founder. He took Nvidia to fame and fortune through a series of tremendous bets. In 1996, three years after he cofounded the company at a Denny’s diner, Nvidia nearly went out of business while working on a failed graphics chip for the Sega Dreamcast game console. But even though he didn’t deliver that chip, Huang personally convinced Sega to invest $5 million afterward, The Wall Street Journal reported in 2024. He then turned around and bet the company again on the Riva 128 PC graphics accelerator, an effort so ambitious he had to lay off over half of Nvidia’s roughly 100 staffers, skip the prototyping stage, and rush it straight to production, and he still only had one month of payroll left by the time it shipped, The New Yorker wrote in 2023. Thankfully, it was a success, selling a million units in just four months and paving the way for both the GeForce GPU and a long-term relationship with chip fabricator TSMC. Roughly eight years later, Huang decided it wasn’t enough to be the leader in PC gaming graphics alone. He bet the company’s entire gross profit , he told podcaster Lex Fridman, on shipping a new feature inside those graphics cards that no one had asked for: CUDA. It was the ability to use a GPU for other kinds of computing tasks beyond graphics, and Huang said it increased the cost of every GeForce graphics card by 50 percent. “Originally there was no market or market demand for it. It was almost as if they built it because they could,” says Peddie. “Jensen had the vision for what it could be and the courage to pursue it in spite of the opinions of others.” “NVIDIA was effectively investing in a computing platform that extended far beyond graphics,

sources.title: Asian governments react to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s exit
sources.text: Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia has drawn a range of responses across Asia, with some governments moving to confirm chip supply commitments, while others are monitoring the impact on local projects or addressing ongoing investigations. On Sunday, November 8, Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation after reports that Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation; Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed. Nvidia’s influence extends far beyond the United States. The chip giant has built close ties with companies worldwide, particularly in Asia, where many of its key partners play important roles in the global AI industry. China’s foreign ministry rejected allegations on November 10 that a Chinese businesswoman linked to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was a spy, calling them groundless and a smear against Beijing. On Friday , a spokesperson reiterated opposition to export controls that disrupt global supply chains and stated the ministry was not aware of reports linking restricted Nvidia chips to a Shanghai data center associated with Alice Huang. Huang’s exit has also raised uncertainty over more than $3 billion in Chinese AI computing projects reliant on Nvidia’s restricted processors, according to Reuters. Many of these chips are subject to U.S. export controls, making them difficult for Chinese companies to obtain. In Singapore, authorities seized the passport of Alice Huang, former CEO of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, in June 2025 as part of an investigation into possible false declarations regarding server purchases, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs. The Singapore ministry said police took her passport to ensure she remained available for questioning, as she was not based in Singapore. The investigation examined whether servers shipped from Singapore to Malaysia were later sent to other countries without proper declaration. In February 2026, police found insufficient evidence to establish that Alice Huang had committed offenses related to the suspected false declarations, according to the ministry. However, authorities said she had knowingly provided inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed. She was issued a warning and barred from re-entering Singapore. Her passport was returned that month. Singapore also said it received limited assistance from U.S. authorities despite repeated requests for information about U.S. server maker Supermicro. Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs said its investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals remains ongoing. The ministry did not identify the six individuals or specify their alleged roles in the case. South Korea has close ties to Nvidia, with major chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix playing important roles in supplying memory chips used in its AI processors. Following Huang’s exit, South Korea’s Science Ministry said Nvidia had reaffirmed its plan to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs to the country and to continue joint AI projects. Apart from that, South Korea’s government AI strategy council held an emergency meeting on Friday to assess the potential impact of Huang’s departure on the country’s AI industry, per a local media report. Taiwan’s Economy Minister Kung Ming-shin said Huang’s departure was unlikely to significantly change the growth of the global AI industry, according to local media . Meanwhile, Taipei’s city government said Nvidia’s planned overseas headquarters in the city remained on track despite the leadership change. The company has met its contractual obligations so far, and officials said they would continue to support the project. In Japan, the Industry Ministry said the government would closely monitor Nvidia following Huang’s resignation, describing the chipmaker as an important player in Japan’s AI semiconductor industry, Reuters reported. Deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki said it was too early to assess the impact on the global AI industry, while stressing Japan’s commitment to ensuring a stable supply of semiconductors. Kate Park is a reporter at TechCrunch, with a focus on technology, startups and venture capital in Asia. She previously was a financial journalist at Mergermarket covering M&A, private equity and venture capital. sources.title: Lutnick faces questions over Nvidia spy scandal. His sons' firm has ties to the chipmaker
sources.text: In late September, Cantor Fitzgerald hosted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and other top executives from the chipmaker for investor meetings in New York, according to a Cantor research report reviewed by CNBC. The Wall Street firm liked what it heard. "We continue to view NVDA as the best risk/reward in our coverage," Cantor analyst C.J. Muse and his colleagues wrote in a research report dated Oct. 3 that maintained a $350 price target and overweight rating on the stock. Yet the firm, formerly run by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and now led by his sons, Brandon and Kyle, reported a nearly 50% decline in the number of Nvidia shares it held between September 2025 and March 2026 , according to a CNBC analysis of securities filings that excludes options. Nvidia had been one of the largest stock positions reported in Cantor's filings. The decline coincided with White House and U.S. intelligence officials pressing Lutnick to crack down on Megaspeed , a Singapore-based company suspected of funneling Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence chips to China . Lutnick repeatedly resisted those efforts, Axios reported Nov. 11. By the time Cantor hosted Huang in New York, Lutnick had also received a classified intelligence warning, according to a Nov. 10 Axios report, about Huang's ties to a suspected Chinese spy and had appeared alongside the CEO at a G20 technology summit in North Carolina. Even as Cantor pared back its Nvidia stake, it continued doing business across the chipmaker's AI empire. A CNBC review of securities filings, corporate announcements and Wall Street research found the firm has helped arrange billions of dollars in financing for Nvidia's business partners while maintaining close ties to the chipmaker's leadership. Those ties have drawn fresh scrutiny following Huang's resignation Thursday and Axios' reporting that Lutnick repeatedly resisted a crackdown on companies suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, despite President Donald Trump authorizing new export restrictions on those companies for a third time on Nov. 5. An ethics expert said the relationship between Lutnick and his former firm's investments may raise questions, given what the secretary knew about Nvidia. Richard Painter , the former chief White House ethics lawyer for President George W. Bush and now a corporate law professor at the University of Minnesota, said that while "there's no proof of" Lutnick sharing nonpublic information with Cantor Fitzgerald, "the appearance doesn't look great." "His conversations with his sons better be about publicly available information," Painter told CNBC. There is no evidence that Lutnick's sons had advance knowledge of the intelligence concerns, that changes in Cantor's reported holdings were tied to any warnings or that the firm's business interests influenced their father's decisions. "Cantor has to date from time to time had only immaterial stand-alone proprietary positions in Nvidia, unlike the positions reflected in 13F filings which were entered into in the ordinary course of business in connection with client swap transactions, that are common in institutional markets," a Cantor spokesperson told CNBC. Cantor declined to answer CNBC's other questions. The Commerce Department, the White House, Howard Lutnick, Brandon Lutnick and Kyle Lutnick did not respond to CNBC's requests for comment or detailed questions about the findings. As scrutiny of Huang intensified, Cantor Chairman Brandon Lutnick was publicly praising the chipmaker's leadership. "Nvidia is one of the great companies on the planet, and they have an amazing leadership team," Brandon Lutnick told Fox Business on Wednesday. Trump is standing by Howard Lutnick. A White House official told Reuters on Thursday that the president maintains "complete confidence" in the commerce secretary. But cracks in the administration's unity emerged Friday, when Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC's "Squawk Box" that the departments of Treasury, Defense and State and the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative all "were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months." Bessent pointed to Commerce as the department responsible for imposing the entity list, which identifies restricted businesses and other groups, adding, "You will have to ask them about their internal processes." Nvidia was Cantor's second-largest reported stock position before Howard Lutnick left Wall Street to become commerce secretary in February 2025, behind only bitcoin investor MicroStrategy, now known as Strategy . At the end of 2024, the firm disclosed more than 3.5 million Nvidia shares worth $479 million, according to its quarterly securities filing . That share count held steady through September 2025, but its value climbed 36% to $652 million, according to Cantor's quarterly securities filing , as the Trump administration moved over the summer to ease restrictions on Nvidia's H20 chip sales to China . Over the following six months, however, the number of Nvidia shares Cantor reported holding fell by 49%, to 3 million in December and 1.78 million by the end of March 2026 , with their value dropping from $652 million to $310 million, according to a CNBC analysis of securities filings. Pressure on Howard Lutnick was also mounting on Capitol Hill. Sens. Jim Banks, R-Ind., and Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., in March urged the secretary to suspend or reconsider Nvidia's export licenses after three people linked to Nvidia customer Super Micro Computer were indicted on charges of conspiring to smuggle AI chips to China. "The Trump administration, I think, leaks like a sieve when it comes to nonpublic government information getting to various hedge fund guys," Painter said, though he stressed there is no evidence Howard Lutnick had shared such information with his sons. sources.title: Small nuclear reactors could soon power the next generation of AI data centers — modular reactors could soon power Dow Texas chemical plant
sources.text: No small modular reactor currently operates commercially in the United States Artificial intelligence companies are increasingly turning toward nuclear energy as electricity demand rises alongside expanding computing infrastructure. X-energy has secured federal permission to construct modular reactors at a chemical manufacturing complex in Texas. The approval allows the nuclear startup to bring its technology closer to commercial deployment, although operational reactors remain years away. The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) has authorized construction of four Xe-100 reactors at a Dow industrial facility in Texas. Each unit is designed to generate 80 megawatts (MW) of electricity alongside another 200 MW of thermal energy - so together, the proposed installation would provide 320 MW of electrical generation, giving the chemical manufacturer an additional source of industrial power. X-energy describes the regulatory decision as the first construction authorization for an advanced nuclear installation at an American industrial location. However, receiving permission to begin construction does not mean the reactors are ready to supply electricity for data centers . Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed! The company expects Dow's installation to enter service sometime during the early 2030s, leaving several years before commercial operation begins. The proposed technology uses uranium-bearing fuel pellets, with helium gas circulating through the reactor to carry away generated heat. X-energy argues this arrangement offers safety advantages over conventional nuclear power systems, although independent experts have questioned those assurances. The Union of Concerned Scientists also criticized the regulatory process, particularly the handling of outstanding safety considerations before construction approval. “The NRC only accomplished this feat by pushing consideration of critical safety questions to a later date,” said Edwin Lyman, director of nuclear power safety at the Union of Concerned Scientists. He argued that regulators should have resolved those outstanding concerns before authorizing construction at the industrial location. Demand from artificial intelligence infrastructure operators has given emerging nuclear developers another potential source of commercial interest. Large technology companies need substantial electricity supplies for computing facilities, particularly as increasingly powerful AI systems require additional processing capacity. Conventional electricity providers face growing pressure to accommodate those requirements, creating opportunities for alternative generation technologies. Amazon has become one of X-energy's major financial supporters through its Climate Pledge Fund investment. The technology company led a $500 million Series C-1 financing round in October 2024 and separately committed to purchasing 5 gigawatts of nuclear generating capacity, an agreement which gives X-energy a significant potential customer as it works toward developing commercial reactors. The startup also attracted substantial investor interest through its initial public offering earlier this year, which generated $1 billion in proceeds. However, enthusiasm among investors has moderated since the April listing, suggesting that commercial expectations remain sensitive to development timelines. The company still faces the challenge of turning regulatory permission and financial commitments into functioning electricity-generating infrastructure. Small modular reactors have attracted attention because their developers expect factory-oriented production and smaller installations to simplify construction. Those proposed advantages include shorter development schedules and lower costs, although neither benefit has been conclusively established. No small modular reactor currently operates commercially in the United States, leaving X-energy's proposed installation dependent on successful construction and regulatory oversight. sources.title: Bessent calls for ‘dramatic shakeup’ at Nvidia, urges outside CEO
sources.text: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday called for a "dramatic shakeup" at Nvidia after CEO Jensen Huang 's resignation, questioning whether the chipmaker pursued illicit sales of its advanced artificial intelligence chips to boost earnings. Bessent said Nvidia's board should look outside the company for its next chief executive and suggested other executives should face scrutiny over the chip giant's compliance with U.S. export controls. "I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?" Bessent said in an interview on Fox News. The remarks come amid a growing feud between Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over the suspected diversion of advanced AI chips to China, even as the Treasury secretary continues to defend President Donald Trump's handling of the matter. Both Bessent and Lutnick are expected to accompany Trump to China this week, Semafor reported Sunday, putting the two Cabinet secretaries alongside the president as he prepares to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit. A White House official told Reuters on Thursday that the president maintains "complete confidence" in Lutnick, despite mounting scrutiny of the secretary’s handling of the Nvidia matter. Huang resigned Thursday following revelations about his relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed , whom U.S. intelligence officials suspect of spying for China. Megaspeed is suspected of diverting Nvidia chips to China in violation of U.S. export controls. Nvidia named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO. Bessent suggested Sunday that Nvidia's problems extended well beyond Huang. "If this were a bank and they hadn't complied like this, the OCC would be in there right now, and a lot of the executives would be removed," Bessent said, referring to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. Bessent also questioned Nvidia's financial disclosures, pointing to a surge in reported Singapore revenue as its China sales fell. Nvidia stopped separately reporting Singapore revenue in November 2025, saying a new methodology based on customers' headquarters rather than billing addresses better reflected the geographic distribution of its sales. Bessent's remarks came two days after he told CNBC's "Squawk Box" that several federal agencies had supported adding Megaspeed to the government's export blacklist for months. "But Commerce has the pen," Bessent said. The public rebuke followed reporting by Axios that Bessent confronted Lutnick in the White House Situation Room over Commerce's failure to act against Megaspeed. Commerce denied that the confrontation took place. Lutnick is also facing scrutiny over his family's financial ties to Nvidia. CNBC reported Friday that Cantor Fitzgerald, the Wall Street firm formerly run by Lutnick and now led by his sons, has helped arrange billions of dollars in financing for Nvidia's business partners. Cantor said Nvidia share holdings fell nearly 50% over six months as national security concerns surrounding Huang escalated. The positions were associated with client swap transactions, not proprietary investments, the investment bank said. There is no evidence Lutnick shared sensitive information with his sons or that Cantor traded on such information. Bessent on Sunday said Trump had drawn a firm line against sales of chips more advanced than Nvidia's H200 to China . Trump himself authorized H200 sales to approved Chinese customers in December —following months of lobbying by Huang — in an arrangement under which the U.S. government would receive a 25% cut. Bessent's latest criticism comes two days before Nvidia is scheduled to report its first quarterly earnings since Huang's departure.

stories.title: Train, Evaluate, and Deploy Action Recognition Models with Roboflow
stories.summary: Train an action recognition model in Roboflow on your own labeled video, and get a timeline of every step it sees, with start and end times.

sources.title: Train, Evaluate, and Deploy Action Recognition Models with Roboflow
sources.text: We're announcing support for action recognition in Roboflow, so you can train and deploy vision models that understand what happens over time in videos. An action recognition model can watch a video clip and return a timeline of the actions it detects, with a start and end time for each one. That means you can turn hours of video into a record of what happened, when it happened, and in what order. Roboflow helps teams build vision systems that see the world, understand what's happening, and take action. With action recognition, those systems can detect specific types of actions and record when each one starts and ends in the video. This is useful for teams that need to answer questions about physical actions, like: An action recognition model helps answer those questions by watching video. From there, you can send the output to another system to analyze the actions over time or to trigger alerts and automations based on what the model finds. We trained action recognition models on three public datasets. In each video, the timeline you see at the top shows the ground truth, and the timeline at the bottom is the model's prediction. The model watches two camera views side by side and tracks six short manipulation primitives, including a regrasp, where the robot lets go of a part and picks it up again in a new position. The model splits a long robot session into pick, insert, remove, and place, without being told how many steps to expect. The model follows all 12 steps of a gear train assembly, recorded by a person it never saw in training. Many of the questions operations teams ask are about what happens over time. Did the operator do every step, in order? How long did each step take? Did the robot finish its sequence, or retry? Object detection tells you what is in a frame, but a single frame can't answer these. Action recognition looks at a window of frames, so it sees the motion. It works well for: It also turns footage you already record into data: run a model over a week of video and you get a timestamp for every step of every cycle. Roboflow supports two action recognition models, Cosmos 3 Edge and V-JEPA 2.1. Both look at a video in 16-second windows and label each moment in a window with one of your actions. On longer videos, the window slides along the clip, and the results are merged into one timeline. We trained both on three public datasets and scored them on test videos the models hadn’t seen in training. The F1 score below counts a predicted action as correct when it overlaps the true action by at least half, and mIoU (mean intersection over union) measures how closely the predicted start and end times match the true ones. V-JEPA 2.1 was more accurate on every dataset. Cosmos 3 Edge often placed the start and end of each action a bit more precisely, which can matter if you care about exact step timing. Results on your data will differ, so try both. Roboflow Training bills 2 credits per GPU hour, so the gear train run cost about 16 credits with V-JEPA 2.1. Training either model yourself means a 24 GB or larger GPU and hours to days of babysitting a run. Here's how to go from raw videos to a deployed model. In app.roboflow.com , click "New Project" and pick "Action Recognition" as the project type. Upload your videos, open one from "Annotate", and mark time ranges instead of drawing boxes. The editor shows the clip on top and one timeline row per action. Drag across a row from where the action starts to where it ends, and drag either edge to adjust. To go faster, run Auto Label on a batch: name the actions, describe when each one happens, and review the segments it finds. Our gear train dataset had 82 videos from 41 people: 29 for training, 6 for validation, and 6 for testing. Create a dataset version, click "Train on This Version", and pick a model. V-JEPA 2.1 is in Beta on paid plans. We trained both on the same version: on the gear train test set, V-JEPA 2.1 reached 87.3% accuracy after about 8 hours of training, and Cosmos 3 Edge 80.0% after about 12. The "Ready to train" panel shows a cost estimate, and you can set a credit cap. You can try the endpoint before you train anything. Install the SDK with pip install -U inference-sdk and send a clip to the base Cosmos 3 Edge model: On the first 45 seconds of a gear train assembly, the base model has no classes of its own, so it describes what it sees: When your training finishes, replace model_id with your model's ID (it looks like your-project/2 ). Our fine-tuned model on the same clip: Every step is named with your classes, in order, with start and end times. For live cameras, add the Action Recognition Model (opens in a new tab) block to a Workflow, or run the model on your own GPUs with Roboflow Inference (opens in a new tab) . Create an Action Recognition project, label a few dozen clips, and train your first model today. Sign up for Roboflow to get started, or talk to sales about running it across your lines and sites. Learn more in the Action Recognition docs (opens in a new tab) .
